title: What If Pet Snakes Took Over a Swamp? Florida's Did

scenes.text: What if pet snakes took over an entire national park? In Florida's Everglades, they did.
Burmese pythons from Southeast Asia, spread by the pet trade, were officially established there by 2000.
They eat birds, mammals and even alligators.
Between the 1990s and 2003 to 2011, raccoon sightings in the park fell by 99.3 percent.
Opossum sightings dropped 98.9 percent. Bobcats fell 87.5 percent.
Only small rodents held steady. Where pythons lived longest, the losses were worst.

description:
What if pet snakes took over a swamp?
In Florida's Everglades, Burmese pythons wiped out almost all raccoons and opossums seen in surveys.
